newsitem.title: USA: Weather Express sees rain next week in central Ill.
newsitem.headline: Weather Express sees rain next week in central Ill.

text.p: A tropical storm developing in the U.S. Gulf could bring widespread rains next week to parched portions of central and southern Illinois, Weather Express Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser said.

"Moisture from what should become Tropical Storm Danny is in a position to provide 0.50 to 2.00-plus inches with 80 percent coverage for Missouri and southern Illinois up to Peoria on Monday," Gesser said.
Recent storms have bypassed central Illinois, leaving some areas in dire need of moisture. The lack of rainfall pushed CBOT corn futures higher this week.
Other private forecasters have predicted the southern U.S. Corn Belt would remain hot and dry through early next week with only scattered showers expected.

Gesser said a cold front would move across the western U.S. Midwest on Sunday, bringing 0.50 to 1.50 inches of rain with 60 percent coverage to parts of Nebraska, Iowa and Minnesota. That cold front will likely meet up with moisture from the tropical system on Monday, he said.
"This tropical system is making everything look wet," Gesser said. "That should include portions of Ohio and Indiana on Tuesday."
